title: Borealis Health — Data Protections & Training Assurance
next_steps: Redwood to share latest SOC 2 Type II report and ISO cert by 2025-06-20
Customer to send completed security questionnaire by 2025-06-24
Schedule hands-on pilot network test in VPC with BOR-Eng on 2025-06-30
action_items: Alex Mercer - share SOC2 + ISO artifacts (2025-06-20)
Samira Khan - provide KMS key flow diagram and HSM/BYOK docs (2025-06-20)
Priya Desai - send completed security questionnaire and list of required compliance clauses (2025-06-24)
Jin Wu - set up short demo of audit log export to customer's SIEM (follow-up meeting)
meeting_header: Date: 2025-06-18 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~42m | Hosted by: Alex Mercer (Redwood AE) | Redwood attendees: Alex Mercer, Samira Khan, Jin Wu | Customer: Borealis Health - Priya Desai (Head of Security), Ethan Ross (CTO), Marta Alvarez (Legal Counsel), Liam O'Neal (Platform)
summary: Focused security review covering SOC 2/ISO artifacts, RBAC/SSO, audit logs, encryption/KMS, data residency and explicit confirmation that customer prompts/content are not used to train models. Action items include sharing certs, KMS diagrams, questionnaire and scheduling pilot VPC test.
topics: SOC 2 Type II evidence; ISO 27001 status; SSO/SAML and Okta integration; RBAC roles and least privilege; audit log retention/export; data residency options and region pinning; encryption at rest and in transit, KMS/BYOK/HSM; prompt retention and 'no training' assurance on customer data; PII/PHI handling and HIPAA/BAA conversation; retention policies and ability to opt-out of analytics/usage logging; legal DPA and contractual controls
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Mercer: alright folks thanks for joining, we have about 40 minutes, um, quick roll call — Alex from Redwood, Samira and Jin on engineering. Priya, Ethan, Marta and Liam from Borealis — can you hear us okay?
[00:08] Priya Desai: yes loud and clear, thanks. we wanted to focus this session on two things — how data flows, and a hard confirmation that customer content won't be used to train models. also a couple follow up Qs on encryption and audit logs.
[00:18] Samira Khan: great, we'll start with the high-level compliance pack — Redwood has a SOC 2 Type II audit in the last 12 months, and an ISO 27001 certification, both available. i'll drop links after the call.
[00:28] Marta Alvarez: is that full cert or just a gap report? we need evidence for our procurement.
[00:32] Alex Mercer: good call — it's the full Type II report and the ISO cert; we can provide redacted copies and the auditor letter.
[00:38] Ethan Ross: redaction is fine but we need the AICPA attestation page, ok.
[00:42] Jin Wu: on technical controls, i'll cover auth, keys, and logs — on auth we support SAML 2.0 SSO (Okta, OneLogin), SCIM for user provisioning, and RBAC with pre-defined roles — admin, developer, observer, billing — and custom roles via the console.
[00:56] Priya Desai: for roles can you do scoped roles to limit HIPA... HIPAA-relevant scopes? we need least privilege for PHI access.
[01:04] Samira Khan: yes you can scope routes per role; for private deployments we can map to customer groups and enforce segregation. there's also field-level redaction in the request/response pipeline if needed.
[01:15] Liam O'Neal: quick q on SSO lifecycles — if a user leaves, how immediate is deprovisioning? we integrate with SCIM so removal is usually TTL under a minute for tokens to expire, active sessions can be revoked from console. there is some lag for long-lived sessions but revocation is available.
[01:33] Alex Mercer: next, encryption and KMS — we encrypt at transit (TLS 1.2/1.3) and at rest using AES-256. customers can use Redwood-managed keys or bring-your-own-key (BYOK) with a KMS integration; for the strictest controls we support HSM-backed keys and customer-managed keys in supported clouds.
[01:49] Marta Alvarez: do we rotate keys automatically? where are the keys stored when BYOK is used?
[01:54] Jin Wu: rotation is supported and auditable. with BYOK the key material stays in your KMS/HSM and we only receive a wrapped key or allow remote crypto operations depending on the integration. that way raw key material isn't stored in Redwood.
[02:07] Priya Desai: can you confirm that customer data is not used to train models? in writing is preferable — we need contractual assurance.
[02:15] Alex Mercer: short version: we do not use customer prompts or content to train or fine-tune models for the hosted product, unless explicit opt-in is agreed and documented. for dedicated/private deployments the customer controls training entirely. we'll include this clause in the DPA and the security artifact bundle.
[02:33] Marta Alvarez: okay we want exact language for our legal team.
[02:36] Alex Mercer: noted — action item: we'll share the exact no-training clause.
[02:40] [00:03] Ethan Ross: you mentioned logs — what's captured in audit logs and retention?
[02:45] Samira Khan: audit logs capture login events, API calls (including route, model, token usage), key management events, and admin actions; we do not log full request/response payloads by default in audit logs for security reasons, but there's a separate request logs option for debug which is configurable and can be routed to a customer's SIEM.
[03:05] Liam O'Neal: retention windows? default vs configurable?
[03:08] Jin Wu: default audit log retention is 90 days on hosted, exportable as compressed JSON/CSV. for Dedicated/Private you can set retention to match your policy and we have a facility to forward logs to your storage or SIEM (S3, Splunk, Datadog).
[03:19] Priya Desai: we need immutable audit trails for 7 years for certain workflows — do you support WORM-style retention or append-only logs?
[03:26] Samira Khan: for hosted it's more limited; for Dedicated/Private we can support write-once storage via your cloud S3 with object lock or by routing into a third-party archive. we'll detail the architecture in the follow-up docs.
[03:38] Marta Alvarez: what about data residency — is there region pinning? we can't send PHI outside the EU for some workloads.
[03:44] Alex Mercer: yes region pinning is supported on Dedicated and Private. Hosted API has regional endpoints and we can pin volumes to EU regions for enterprise plans; for absolute residency guarantees we recommend Private deployment in your VPC.
[03:56] Priya Desai: the big one for us — prompt retention and PII/PHI handling. what retention is applied to raw prompts and responses?
[04:05] Jin Wu: by default, request logs are stored for 30 days for diagnostics; prompts/responses used for telemetry are pseudo-anonymized and aggregated. however, if you enable "no retention" mode on your account or choose Private, we can disable storage of prompts entirely. we also provide a redaction API to mask PII before it leaves your environment.
[04:24] Ethan Ross: pseudo-anonymized — can you clarify? how reversible is that?
[04:27] Samira Khan: pseudo-anonymization removes direct identifiers and hashes unique tokens, but it's not guaranteed irreversible for highly structured PHI; for strict PHI handling you should use redaction + Private deployment or pre-processing on your side.
[04:41] Priya Desai: HIPAA/BBA — will Redwood sign a BAA for the hosted product?
[04:47] Alex Mercer: Redwood can sign a BAA for Dedicated and Private deployments; for hosted we have customers on a per-case basis — we need to take it through legal review. we'll include our standard DPA and then escalate BAA discussion with legal.
[04:58] Marta Alvarez: ok please flag that as high priority.
[05:01] [00:05] Liam O'Neal: on-the-fly question: what about model fallbacks and routing? if a request is routed to a cheaper model, does that change data handling assumptions?
[05:08] Jin Wu: good catch — routing policies are configured per-tenant. all models in the catalog follow the same data handling rules; if you route to external, third-party model providers (not in Redwood) we make that explicit and the contract will reflect their training policies.
[05:22] Priya Desai: are there any telemetry tags that leak PII into ML features?
[05:26] Samira Khan: telemetry is token-level counts and latency metrics; we don't include prompt text in telemetry. that said, we maintain strict controls — but we will add a note about turning off telemetry for your tenant during the pilot.
[05:38] Alex Mercer: quick demo offer — Jin can show a live audit log export to S3 and we'll simulate a redaction rule later. would you want this in the pilot?
[05:46] Ethan Ross: yes, that helps. we want to see the export shape to map to our SIEM.
[05:50] Marta Alvarez: also need the exact legal clause re: no training + DPA language.
[05:54] Alex Mercer: understood. we'll attach the clause and the SOC/ISO artifacts.
[05:59] [00:06] Priya Desai: one final Q — where are backups stored and how are they encrypted?
[06:04] Jin Wu: backups are stored in encrypted object storage, same region as your primary data plane unless you opt for cross-region replication. backups are encrypted with keys under your control if BYOK is enabled.
[06:16] Liam O'Neal: for the pilot we want a VPC private deployment and BYOK with rotation every 90 days, and audit logs exported to our Splunk instance.
[06:25] Alex Mercer: noted — we'll scope that in the pilot plan.
[06:28] Marta Alvarez: legal will review the DPA + BAA possibility, i'll turn around a redline if needed.
[06:33] Alex Mercer: cool, recap and next steps: we'll send SOC2/ISO, KMS diagrams, no-training clause, and set the pilot date. any blockers?
[06:42] Priya Desai: no blockers, just need the docs to close procurement. thanks.
[06:46] Alex Mercer: great, thank you everyone. we'll follow up in email with attachments and schedule. bye.
[06:50] [END]
